page: Amazon Web Services c6a.48xlarge is a high-density, compute-optimized instance driven by the AWS Nitro System and 3rd Generation AMD EPYC 7R13 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 192 dedicated vCPUs across 96 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at clock speeds up to 3.6 GHz. Memory capacity is configured at 384.0 GB of DDR4 running at 3 GHz, establishing a focused 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core). The instance does not feature local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, operating with external storage attachments over a 50 Gbps baseline network fabric.

Performance benchmarks confirm high multi-core throughput, placing the c6a.48xlarge in the top tier for multi-threaded CPU operations, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 286,847.44 and a PassMark CPU rating of 114,279.25. Hardware cryptography benchmarks demonstrate high throughput with 218,639.67 on PassMark CPU encryption tests, while memory subsystem benchmarks indicate high-speed small-block cached reads at 11,810.7 GB/sec. It also demonstrates exceptional throughput in distributed key-value workloads, registering 178.04 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core metrics remain closer to median levels, and AVX-512 extensions are absent.

In terms of infrastructure economics, the instance provides high compute density per socket without the expense of bundled high-capacity local drives or accelerators. Workloads relying on heavy parallelization achieve favorable cost-to-performance efficiency. Best-fit use cases include parallel software compilation, ray tracing rendering pipelines, high-traffic static web servers, distributed batch processing, and memory-cached database layers.
description: Amazon Web Services c6a.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by 3rd generation AMD EPYC 7R13 processors on the x86_64 architecture. Managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the platform provides 192 dedicated vCPUs across 96 physical cores running at up to 3.6 GHz, coupled with 384 GB of DDR4-3000 memory maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It provides a baseline network throughput of 50 Gbps but includes no local storage or discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight exceptional multi-threaded compute and in-memory processing, scoring in the top tier for stress-ng multi-core execution, PassMark CPU tests, and Redis SET operations surpassing 178 million operations per second. Single-threaded metrics and non-AVX-512 vector execution perform at median levels. The c6a.48xlarge is engineered for compute-heavy parallel workloads, including distributed build systems, ray tracing, large-scale Redis deployments, and continuous integration pipelines requiring high CPU density.
